rubric.CLOSED: a published paper OR a live public tool computes essentially this quantity as a single number characterising a MODEL, parent-free, and uses it to compare, rank or score checkpoints. Verbatim quote required.
rubric.PARTIAL: the quantity exists but fails exactly one of: per-input rather than per-checkpoint; needs a parent/reference; never scalarised; exists only outside safety; never scored against anything.
rubric.OPEN: >=3 distinct query families with zero relevant hits AND >=1 positive-control-backed zero-match regex on the nearest-neighbour paper. Anything weaker is PARTIAL.

rows.definition: Site-local write gain: project the model's own fitted request axis F out at an early band b (last prompt token); |delta proj onto late-band r_late| minus a matched-norm orthogonalised random-direction control.
rows.quantity_described: No work found that ablates a fitted axis at an EARLY band, reads the effect on a DIFFERENT, LATE-band refusal direction's mean projection, and subtracts a matched-norm random-direction control, as a single per-checkpoint scalar. Nearest neighbors (Arditi et al. single-direction ablation graphs, the LessWrong per-layer study, Galeone's detection-vs-intervention cosine) either ablate and read at the SAME site, or compare two fitted axes rather than an early-ablation's causal effect on a late fixed axis with a random-control baseline.
rows.regex_used: query families: 'intervention-response score per model activation direction' (10 hits, none matching); '"write handle" vs readable direction language model' (10 hits, none matching); 'causal effect of ablating a direction as a MODEL-level score' (1 hit, irrelevant); plus zero-match regex 'matched-norm random|random-direction control' on arXiv:2606.24952 PDF (0/55834 chars)
rows.positive_control: pattern 'detection' on arXiv:2606.24952 PDF returned 104 matches in same session

rows.definition: Redundancy depth: smallest k in 1..6 such that JOINT ablation of k bands halves the r_late projection; censored at 7.
rows.quantity_described: SafeSeek finds a minimal-sparsity circuit (0.42% / 3.03%+0.79%) via gradient-optimized masks, per model/scenario, whose joint ablation collapses a behavior -- but the granularity is heads/neurons via optimization, not a fixed 6-layer-band k-search, and it is not scored across multiple checkpoints as a ranking/comparison metric. The LessWrong post jointly ablates 31-of-32 layers vs all 32 and finds near-identical ASR, but on a SINGLE model, with 3 fixed conditions (not a k-search), and is a non-peer-reviewed blog post.
rows.quote: localizing an alignment circuit with 3.03% heads and 0.79% neurons, whose removal spikes ASR from 0.8% to 96.9%
rows.regex_used: redundan|checkpoint|across model|multiple model|compare.{0,20}model|rank on arxiv.org/html/2603.23268v1 (3 matches, all irrelevant -- LoRA rank / citations, no cross-checkpoint comparison use)

rows.definition: Positional redundancy ratio: all-position ablation effect / last-prompt-token-only ablation effect, same band.

rows.definition: Self-repair coefficient: after ablating F's component at band b, the fraction of the removed component written back by the layers above b by the end of the stack.
rows.quote: We recast this failure as a recovery task, conditional circuit completion, and introduce Conditional Co-Ablation (CoAx), a label-free, output-grounded score that asks how much each remaining unit's ablation effect grows once a primary set has been removed.
rows.rationale: The full forward-citation sweep on both anchors (Semantic Scholar Graph API, 100+36=136 citing papers scanned with 5 distinct regex passes across the two anchors) is now complete and confirms no work reduces self-repair/backup behaviour to a per-checkpoint scalar used to compare, rank, or score model checkpoints. The two retried query families ('compensation coefficient ablation transformer layers' and 'how much of an ablated component is written back downstream') also returned zero relevant hits, backed by a positive control ('hydra effect language model self-repair', re-run in the same session, correctly surfaced the real McGrath et al. paper at position 1 of 10 -- proving the search backend was functioning and the other two queries' irrelevant results are true negatives, not backend failure). The nearest-neighbour paper (CoAx, arXiv:2607.01940) was tested with a zero-match regex for checkpoint/cross-checkpoint framing (0/140365 chars) with a working positive control on the same URL in the same session (143 matches for 'ablation'). The OPEN bar (>=3 distinct query families with zero relevant hits, AND >=1 positive-control-backed zero-match regex on the nearest-neighbour paper) is now met with margin: distinct zero-relevant-hit families are (1) 'backup heads redundancy transformer circuit', (2) 'self-repair across models comparison', (3) 'self-repair metric checkpoint', (4) 'compensation coefficient ablation transformer layers', (5) 'how much of an ablated component is written back downstream', (6) 'anti-erasure/negative head self-repair' (1 low-quality non-scalarising hit), plus (7) the citation sweep itself as an independent, exhaustive-within-both-anchors check. No CLOSED-worthy source was found in any of these, so the verdict does not soften to PARTIAL and does not upgrade to CLOSED -- it holds at OPEN.

rows.definition: Decode-site write gain: W1 read at the model's own first 1-8 greedy decode positions.
rows.quantity_described: Any-Depth Alignment is the general precedent for reading safety signal at decode positions rather than the prompt (t-SNE separability of Safety-Token hidden states increases with generation depth d; linear probe ADA(LP) reads harmfulness from decode-position hidden states). It does not perform the specific write-gain construction (early-band ablation -> late-band projection-change minus random-direction control), is per-input/per-generation, not aggregated into a single per-checkpoint ranking scalar, and uses probes/re-injection rather than ablation.

rows.quote: As generation depth increases, features from injected Safety Tokens (bottom) – where we read the hidden state of the assistant token from the assistant header – become highly separable, while those from the last generated token (top) remain entangled.

rows.definition: Rotation under self-lesion: cosine between the model's own F before and after its own fixed-strength rank-one self-lesion of o_proj/down_proj.
rows.quantity_described: Jorak checks whether a CURRENTLY-fitted r-hat still projects onto the (possibly already-ablated) weight matrix (r^T W' ~= 0 test), a detection statistic, not a self-administered lesion followed by REFITTING the axis and measuring its rotation. OBLITERATUS's CrossLayerAlignmentAnalyzer computes cosine drift of the SAME (unablated) direction ACROSS LAYERS in one forward pass, not BEFORE vs AFTER a self-lesion of the SAME layer. Neither tool performs the self-lesion + refit + before/after cosine workflow that W8 specifies.

rows.definition: Used-ness: cosine between the fitted axis and the residual delta the band's own layers write on harmful prompts.
rows.quantity_described: Galeone computes cos(d_det, d_ref): the angle between a detection axis (probe/DiM direction for a property) and an INTERVENTION/steering axis that was chosen to CAUSE the behavior -- not the angle between the fitted axis and the layer's OWN naturally-computed residual-stream update on harmful prompts absent any intervention. Same family of per-checkpoint, weight-computable, parent-free cosine scalar, and explicitly shown to be non-predictive of steerability -- but a different pair of directions than G3 specifies.
rows.behaviour_named: Fabricates / Refuses / Mixed (steerability outcome per model)
rows.quote: The cosine between detection and intervention is computable from the weights and consistent across four models (cos ∈ [0.12, 0.20], a small but reproducible positive). It is tempting to read it as an a priori steerability test; we show it is not.

rows.definition: Fisher ratio in the subspace orthogonal to the unembedding's refusal-token rows.

No Fisher-ratio / orthogonal-complement construction was found.

obliteratus.name: OBLITERATUS (github.com/elder-plinius/OBLITERATUS), module CrossLayerAlignmentAnalyzer
obliteratus.ruling: It computes a CROSS-LAYER CONSISTENCY / angular-drift scalar (pairwise cosine matrix between per-layer refusal directions, direction_persistence_score, cluster_count, total_geodesic_distance, mean_adjacent_cosine) on a SINGLE model's unablated directions. It does NOT compute a redundancy/joint-ablation scalar: there is no k-of-N joint-ablation search and no 'how many layers must be ablated to collapse behavior' output anywhere in this module's docstring or dataclass fields.
obliteratus.quote: This analysis also reveals "refusal direction clusters" -- groups of layers that share similar refusal geometry ... Contribution: We also compute the "refusal direction flow" -- the cumulative angular drift of the refusal direction through the network, measured as the total geodesic distance on the unit hypersphere.

jorak.name: Jorak Model Scanner (github.com/JolanMc/Jorak, package name 'modelscanner')
jorak.status: RE-LOCATED_LIVE_THIS_SESSION -- the generic web search for 'Jorak Model Scanner' (carried over from prior session, s_SB_jorak1.txt) returned only noise (3D scanners, WoW NPCs), but a targeted query ('jorak model scanner github safety scar') and a direct README fetch of github.com/JolanMc/Jorak this session CONFIRMED the real repository and its exact metrics.
jorak.ruling: Confirmed live, real, open-source, non-peer-reviewed. It ships exactly the described normalised r^T W suppression statistic (global alignment A and band alignment B) and a weights-only SVD subspace-alignment scar test (subspace alignment S, bottom-k shared subspace), computed per model from safetensors weights with no reference/parent model, classified into 4 provenance buckets and plotted/compared across models via a `compare` CLI. It is the correct real-world referent for the run's prior 'Jorak' summary; nothing about it needs to be treated as unverifiable.
jorak.quote: Weights — spectral signature (SVD) (the smoking-gun, CPU, no inference). Three signals: global alignment A (full ablation), band alignment B (localized/stealthy ablation, Heretic-style), and subspace alignment S (bottom-k shared subspace -- catches multi-direction ablation, e.g. OBLITERATUS n_directions > 1, which a single u_min dilutes).
